The upper positive terminal first passes through a series resistor labeled 2kΩ, then reaches the common output upper node on the right; below is a common negative-terminal bus. The two Zener diodes are connected in parallel at the same output node; the lower-Zener-voltage VZ1 will enter the voltage-stabilizing state first, clamping the output node at 6V; at this time the node voltage does not reach the 8V Zener voltage of VZ2, so VZ2 does not have a clamping effect.
